instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA. Cada registro trae su texto
literal completo, el documento y la ruta de encabezados donde está, y a veces un contexto (encabezado de tabla o de
bloque). El encabezado dice el alcance: modelo, régimen, etapa, caso. Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si es un ejemplo o una
  explicación sin norma, empieza con "Ejemplo:" o "Explicación:".
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente según texto y encabezado (modelo y versión, caso, etapa, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata.
Lista de temas (clave: descripción):

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity

registros.texto:
The tables above grade each check as pass, soft fail, or hard fail. The JSON critique
records a severity instead, and the verdict is derived from those severities. Map them
this way, and only this way:

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity

registros.texto: | Soft fail on any layer | `minor` | Post can absorb it. `fix_type` is usually `post-level` |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity

registros.texto: | Hard fail **with** a clear fix path | `major` | A prompt change or a re-roll resolves it |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity

registros.texto: | Hard fail on Brand Lock or Series Lock **with no** fix path | `blocking` | Nothing downstream recovers this |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity

registros.texto: | Any defect that makes the asset unusable | `blocking` | Same, regardless of layer |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict

registros.texto: The verdict follows from the severities. It is not a separate judgement:

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict

registros.texto: | any `blocking` | REJECT |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict

registros.texto: | three or more `major` | REJECT |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict

registros.texto: | one or two `major` | REVISE |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict

registros.texto: | only `minor`, or none | ACCEPT (with post notes) |

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict

registros.texto:
`tools/validate_critique.py` enforces exactly this table, so a critique that disagrees with
it fails rather than shipping. Earlier versions of this file counted hard fails and called
3+ a REJECT while the skill said "escalate at your discretion." Those two rules disagreed,
and the disagreement is the reason the threshold is now a number.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict

registros.texto:
Soft fails are noted but don't change the verdict on their own. If you have three or more of
them, look again: a cluster of soft fails usually means one of them is really a hard fail
you talked yourself out of.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember

registros.texto: - **Don't critique what wasn't asked**, if the spec didn't call for cinematic mood, don't say "could be more cinematic"

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember

registros.texto: - **Don't pile-on once verdict is set**, if you're rejecting, list the issues that drive the rejection; don't list every cosmetic concern

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember

registros.texto: - **Be specific, always**, "lighting is off" is not a critique; "key light is camera-right but series_lock says camera-left" is

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember

registros.texto: - **Cite the layer**, every issue gets tagged with which layer it falls under. This makes the fix path obvious

ubicaciones.encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember

registros.texto: - **Distinguish prompt failure from generator failure**, if the prompt was fine and the generator produced garbage hands, that's "re-roll required", not "fix the prompt"

ubicaciones.encabezado: Creación Visual — Visual Media › Fundamentos de fotografía › Reglas de composición

registros.texto:
```markdown
## Composición básica

### Regla de tercios
- Divide el encuadre en una retícula de 3×3
- Coloca el sujeto en los puntos de intersección
- Sitúa el horizonte en la línea superior o inferior

### Líneas guía
- Usa líneas para conducir la mirada
- Caminos, ríos, barandales
- Que apunten al sujeto

### Encuadre dentro del encuadre
- Enmarca al sujeto con elementos del primer plano
- Marcos de puerta, ventanas, ramas
- Aporta capas y profundidad

### Simetría y equilibrio
- Simetría perfecta = estabilidad, solemnidad
- Asimetría = dinamismo, tensión
- Equilibra el peso visual

### Espacio negativo
- El vacío refuerza el punto focal
- Da "espacio para respirar" al sujeto
- Estética minimalista
```

registros.texto:

```markdown
## Tipos de plano — Shot Types

### Plano general (Wide Shot)
- Establece la escena
- Muestra el entorno
- El personaje se ve pequeño

### Plano entero (Full Shot)
- Cuerpo completo
- Acción legible
- Luce el vestuario

### Plano medio (Medium Shot)
- De la cintura hacia arriba
- Escenas de diálogo
- Gestualidad de manos

### Primer plano (Close-up)
- De los hombros hacia arriba
- Expresión emocional
- Línea de diálogo importante

### Primerísimo primer plano (Extreme Close-up)
- Detalle de ojos o manos
- Emoción intensa
- Detalle de objeto
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Creación Visual — Visual Media › Fundamentos de animación › Los 12 principios

registros.texto:
```markdown
## Los 12 principios de animación de Disney

1. **Squash & Stretch** (compresión y estiramiento)
   - Conservar el volumen
   - Comunicar peso y elasticidad

2. **Anticipación** (Anticipation)
   - Agacharse antes de saltar
   - Retraer el brazo antes del golpe

3. **Puesta en escena** (Staging)
   - Comunicar la intención con claridad
   - Guiar la mirada del espectador

4. **Directo vs. pose a pose** (Straight Ahead & Pose to Pose)
   - Directo: fluido, orgánico
   - Pose a pose: preciso, controlable

5. **Acción continuada y superpuesta** (Follow Through & Overlapping)
   - El retardo del cabello y la ropa
   - Aporta naturalidad

6. **Entradas y salidas lentas** (Slow In & Slow Out)
   - El movimiento arranca y termina lento
   - Y acelera en medio

7. **Arcos** (Arcs)
   - El movimiento natural es curvo
   - Evita la sensación mecánica

8. **Acción secundaria** (Secondary Action)
   - Micromovimientos además de la acción principal
   - Enriquecen al personaje

9. **Timing** (Timing)
   - El número de cuadros define la velocidad
   - Afecta la sensación de peso

10. **Exageración** (Exaggeration)
    - Más intenso que la realidad
    - Resalta el rasgo distintivo

11. **Dibujo sólido** (Solid Drawing)
    - Entender la estructura tridimensional
    - Peso y equilibrio

12. **Atractivo** (Appeal)
    - Carisma del personaje
    - Que dé ganas de verlo
```

registros.texto:
```markdown
## Principios de edición

### Corte en movimiento
- Cambia de plano durante la acción
- Mantiene la fluidez

### Corte en reposo
- Cambia durante una pausa
- Habitual en escenas de diálogo

### Regla de los 180 grados
- Conserva la posición relativa de los personajes
- Evita cruzar el eje

### J-Cut / L-Cut
- J-Cut: el audio entra antes que la imagen
- L-Cut: la imagen se mantiene después del audio
- Aumentan la fluidez
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: frontmatter › description

registros.texto: description: Generate model-specific prompts from shots.json. Outputs copy-paste-ready prompts for stills (Midjourney, Flux, Ideogram, GPT Image, Nano Banana, Seedream) and motion video (Kling, Veo, Seedance, Hailuo). Also runs a revision mode that reads a critique.json and re-emits prompts for only the failed shots, closing the QA loop. Use when the user asks for image or video prompts, mentions any of those generators, wants AI-generated frames for a storyboard, or hands over shots.json. The prompt half of the pipeline. Composes with storyboard-architect upstream, visual-asset-critic downstream.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge

registros.texto: You are turning structured shot data into prompts that work in production. Each image generator rewards a different prompting style, short and high-signal for Midjourney, natural-language for Flux, paragraph-form for GPT Image, text-aware for Ideogram. A prompt that crushes in one will produce slop in another.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge

registros.texto: This skill adapts. Same shot, different syntax.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › When to use

registros.texto:
Trigger when the user:

- Hands over a `shots.json` (or any structured shot list) and asks for prompts
- Names a specific generator (Midjourney, Flux, Ideogram, GPT Image, Nano Banana, Seedream, Kling, Veo, Seedance, Hailuo)
- Asks for "image prompts," "Midjourney prompts," "AI prompts," "generation prompts" for a storyboard
- Wants the same shot adapted to multiple generators

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › When to use

registros.texto: If the user wants to build a storyboard from scratch (no shots.json yet), use `storyboard-architect` first, then chain into this skill.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › What you produce

registros.texto:
For a given `shots.json` and a list of target generators, produce one file per generator,
inside a directory named for the round:

```
output/prompts/round-1/
├── midjourney.txt          # If targeted
├── flux.txt
├── ideogram.txt
├── gpt-image.txt
├── nano-banana.txt
├── seedream.txt
├── kling.txt               # Motion-aware video, default
├── veo.txt                 # Motion, dialogue/lipsync + native audio
├── seedance.txt            # Motion, multi-shot sequences
└── hailuo.txt              # Motion, budget iteration
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › What you produce

registros.texto:
Round 1 is the first pass. Revision mode writes `output/prompts/round-2/`, and so on.
The round in the path is not decoration: prompt files used to be written to one fixed
path per generator, so round 2 destroyed round 1 and the prompt that actually produced
most of the surviving frames was gone.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › What you produce

registros.texto: Each file is plain text, one prompt per shot, separated by a blank line and a `# shot_NN` comment. Designed for copy-paste workflows, drop into the generator's UI or pipe into an API.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy

registros.texto:
Every prompt is composed from these layers. Read `references/prompt-anatomy.md` for the full theory. Quick version:

1. **Brand Lock**, palette, type, mood, "never" list (constant across project)
2. **Series Lock**, character/environment/lighting anchors (constant across storyboard)
3. **Shot Spec**, framing, angle, motion, subject (per shot)
4. **Text Layer**, **never in the prompt**, composited separately
5. **Generator Adapter**, model-specific syntax wrapper

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy

registros.texto: The first four come from `shots.json` and the brand-lock. The fifth is what this skill applies.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 1. Read inputs

registros.texto:
You need:

- `shots.json` (required), the structured shot list
- `brand-lock.snapshot.md` (required), referenced from shots.json
- Target generators (required), ask if not specified

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 1. Read inputs

registros.texto:
Validate before composing:

```bash
python tools/validate_shots.py output/
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 1. Read inputs

registros.texto:
If the brand-lock is missing or `shots.json` does not validate, stop and tell the user.
Don't try to forge prompts from incomplete data.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 1. Read inputs

registros.texto:
If `tools/` is not on hand (a Claude.ai upload, or a single-skill install), read the
schema from `../storyboard-architect/templates/shots.schema.json` and check by hand. That
relative path only resolves when the skills sit side by side; when they don't, ask the
user for the schema rather than composing from memory of it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters

registros.texto:
For each target generator, read the matching adapter file:

- `adapters/midjourney.md`
- `adapters/flux.md`
- `adapters/ideogram.md`
- `adapters/gpt-image.md`
- `adapters/nano-banana.md`
- `adapters/seedream.md`
- `adapters/kling.md`      (motion video, default)
- `adapters/veo.md`        (motion video, dialogue/lipsync + native audio)
- `adapters/seedance.md`   (motion video, multi-shot sequences)
- `adapters/hailuo.md`     (motion video, budget iteration)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters

registros.texto: Each adapter file documents the prompting style, parameter syntax, and known pitfalls for that generator. You **must** read the adapter before writing prompts for it. Don't guess from training data, image-gen syntax has churned multiple times.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters

registros.texto: **`adapters/_capabilities.json` is the single source of truth for per-generator limits** (`max_prompt_words`, `supports_text_render`, `supports_motion`, `aspect_param`, and so on). Read it once at the start and respect those values when composing, and do not target motion on a stills-only generator.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters

registros.texto:
`max_prompt_words` is a ceiling. The range in an adapter `.md` is the recommended target
and always sits inside that ceiling, so a `.md` saying "40 to 70 words" under a ceiling of
120 is guidance, not a conflict. Where a fact in a `.md` and a fact in the JSON genuinely
disagree, **the JSON wins**.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters

registros.texto:
That rule is now enforced rather than trusted. `tools/validate_capabilities.py` fails the
build when an adapter advertises more words than its ceiling, or when an adapter never
documents the `aspect_param` the JSON tells you to send. The second check exists because
nano-banana's matrix entry said `aspect_ratio` while its adapter said the API expects
`aspectRatio`; the precedence rule meant the wrong one won, silently, on every prompt.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 3. Compose per shot

registros.texto:
For each shot in `shots.json`, for each target generator:

1. Pull brand-lock palette, mood, "never" list
2. Pull series_lock character/environment/lighting
3. Pull shot framing/angle/motion/subject
4. **Strip any on_screen_text reference**, text never goes in the prompt
5. Apply the generator adapter's syntax wrapper
6. Append generator-specific parameters (aspect ratio, style flags, seed if applicable)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4. Write output files
Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4. Write output files

registros.texto:
The `#` lines are comments; the user copies just the prompt body. `tools/copy-prompt.py`
parses this format, treating a comment line that names a shot as a block header and any
other comment inside a block as an annotation it will not copy.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4. Write output files

registros.texto:
Record the run and round in the header, not a wall-clock "Generated" line. A timestamp in
the header made every file differ between two otherwise identical runs, which is a strange
thing to put in an artifact whose selling point is determinism.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json

registros.texto:
After writing the files, append an entry to `run.json`'s `rounds` array: the round number,
`started_at`, a `reason`, and for each file its generator, path, SHA-256, and the shot ids
it covers.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json

registros.texto:
```bash
shasum -a 256 output/prompts/round-1/*.txt
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json

registros.texto:
This is the only writeable part of `run.json`. Everything else was fixed when the
architect wrote it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off

registros.texto:
Tell the user where the files are. Offer the next step:

> "Want me to QA the generated images against the storyboard? Use `visual-asset-critic` once you have the renders."

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off

registros.texto:
For paste-into-generator workflows, the user can pipe individual shots to the clipboard with the bundled helper:

```bash
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-1/midjourney.txt
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-2/revised-midjourney.txt --shot shot_03
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off

registros.texto: This is optional. The `.txt` files are also directly readable, and the user can copy any block by hand. The helper exists for the case where the operator is bouncing between the terminal and a generator UI repeatedly.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop)

registros.texto: This is what `visual-asset-critic`'s structured output is for. When the user hands you `shots.json` plus one or more `critique.json` files (the machine-readable verdict the critic writes), don't re-forge the whole storyboard, re-emit prompts for **only the shots that failed**, with the fix already applied.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Trigger

registros.texto: The user says "apply the critique", "revise the failed shots", "re-roll what didn't pass", or hands over an output tree containing `critiques/`.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow

registros.texto:
1. Read every critique under `output/critiques/round-{N}/`, where N is the highest round
   present. Each file is one shot's verdict (`shot_id`, `verdict`, `issues[]`).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow

registros.texto: 2. Skip any with `verdict: ACCEPT`. Those are done.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow

registros.texto:
3. **Stop on `REJECT`.** A REJECT means the critic found a blocking issue, or three or more
   major ones: a failure with no clear fix path. Re-emitting a prompt for it pretends
   otherwise. List the rejected shots, say what the critic said about them, and ask the
   user how to proceed. Common answers are a change to the shot spec, a change to the
   brand-lock, or a different generator, and all three are decisions above this skill's
   pay grade.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow

registros.texto:
4. For every `REVISE` shot, walk its `issues[]` and branch on `fix_type`:
   - **`prompt-level`**, recompose that shot's prompt with the change in `fix` applied
     (e.g. add the missing series_lock anchor). Re-emit it.
   - **`re-roll`**, keep the prompt identical; the generation was just a bad sample.
     Re-emit it with a `# fix [Technical, re-roll]` annotation saying to take 2-3 samples
     and pick the cleanest.
   - **`post-level`**, do **not** re-emit. The fix happens in compositing, not a new
     generation.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow

registros.texto:
5. A shot whose issues are all `post-level` needs no new prompt. Leave it out of the
   revised file and add its id to `post_only_shots` on the new round entry in `run.json`.
   Saying it in chat is not recording it: that obligation has to exist on disk or the
   compositing step is a memory.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow

registros.texto: 6. Re-apply the five-layer anatomy and the same adapter as the original run.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output

registros.texto:
Write `output/prompts/round-{N+1}/revised-{generator}.txt` containing only the revised
shots, then append the round to `run.json`. Annotate each shot with what changed and why,
citing the issue:

```
# shot_03, reframe, 11.0-16.0s, MCU eye-level push, revision (was REVISE)
# fix [Series Lock, major]: added 'salt-and-pepper hair' to the character anchor (was missing)
# fix [Shot Spec, minor]: medium shot -> medium close-up
{the revised prompt}
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output

registros.texto:
The block header leads with the shot id, same as a full pass. `tools/copy-prompt.py`
identifies a block by the shot id near the start of the line, so a header that led with
"Revision of" produced a file the paste helper could not read at all, which is
inconvenient in the one file the operator is about to paste from repeatedly.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output

registros.texto:
Tell the user which shots were revised, which need only post work, which were rejected,
and which were already ACCEPT. Then they generate the revised shots and run
`visual-asset-critic` again.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits

registros.texto:
Given the same `shots.json`, the same brand-lock, and the same critique, this should
produce the same revised prompt. Nothing in the file format fights that any more: no
wall-clock stamps, no random ordering.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits

registros.texto:
What the format cannot guarantee is the judgement in between. Applying a `fix` field means
reading a sentence of English and editing prose, so hold yourself to the narrowest edit
that satisfies the fix and leave every other layer byte-identical. If you find yourself
rewriting a prompt the critique did not ask you to touch, stop: that is drift, and it will
read as a mystery six shots later.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules

registros.texto: These are non-negotiable. Violating them produces broken output even if the prompt looks fine.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 1. Text is never in the prompt

registros.texto: If the shot has `on_screen_text: "text_03"`, the prompt does NOT contain the text content. Text is composited separately. The only exception: Ideogram, where text-in-image is the reason you'd choose it, but even then, treat it as an explicit override flagged in rationale.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 2. Brand colors never in shot subject prose

registros.texto: Colors come from the series_lock color_grade and the brand_lock palette. They get rendered into the prompt by the adapter. Don't write "deep navy blazer" in the shot subject if "deep navy" is already in the palette, that's a duplicated description and produces oversaturation.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

registros.texto:
The series_lock `environment`, `lighting`, and `color_grade` strings flow into every
prompt **verbatim**. This is what produces visual consistency across shots. If you
paraphrase or vary, shots stop matching each other.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

registros.texto:
Verbatim means the whole string, unedited. Not "the same idea in better prose". The
failure mode is specific and easy to walk into: you are writing fluent descriptive
English, `environment` is "minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, single
houseplant", and it reads more naturally as "a minimal home office with white walls and
an oak desk". That is drift. The frames stop matching, and it stays invisible until you
line up six shots and see six different rooms.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

registros.texto:
Capitalising the first letter to start a sentence is fine, because the check is
case-insensitive. "Minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, single houseplant."
satisfies the rule and reads like a sentence. Nothing else may change: no reordering, no
dropped clause, no synonym, no inserted adjective.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

registros.texto:
`character` is a warning rather than an error, because a shot with no person in it can
legitimately leave it out. When the shot has a person, it is verbatim too.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

registros.texto:
This rule is enforced now, not trusted:

```bash
python tools/validate_prompts.py output/
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

registros.texto:
It exists because a careful authoring pass over a seven-shot storyboard drifted on these
anchors in all seven shots while every other validator stayed green.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 4. Adapters are the source of truth on syntax

registros.texto: If your training data says Midjourney uses `--style 4a` and the adapter file says `--style raw`, the adapter wins. Image-gen syntax changes monthly. The adapter is current; your training is not.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry

registros.texto:
A prompt can be beautifully written and still be impossible to shoot. Every prompt declares, before anything else:

- **Where the body sits in frame.** Which third it occupies. On a piece that composites two eras with a vertical mask, a body sitting on the centre line gets split in half and no amount of post fixes it. This is the single most expensive failure in the kit, and it is invisible until the mask goes on.
- **The point of view.** Profile, frontal, side, rear. "A man walking" is not a shot.
- **The direction of travel.** Left to right, right to left, toward camera. Without it the generator picks, and consecutive shots stop matching.
- **Nothing that contradicts the camera.** A subject who walks away from camera cannot also keep the same size in frame.
- **Handedness in any two-person contact.** If one raises a hand, name which one, or you get two right hands meeting.
- **No brand marks.** Logos and lettering are composited in post. Generators deform them.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 5. Prompts must be reproducible

registros.texto: Every prompt is composed from the same inputs the same way. If two consecutive runs produce different prompts for the same shot, the skill is broken. Determinism is the whole point.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar

registros.texto:
Run the validator. Do not eyeball this list.

```bash
python tools/validate_prompts.py output/

```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar

registros.texto:
`validate_prompts.py` checks the mechanical half, which is everything that used to be a
checkbox here:

- the header names the storyboard, generator, aspect, brand-lock, run, and round
- the generator is a real id in `_capabilities.json`
- the header aspect matches `project.aspect`
- no prompt exceeds that generator's `max_prompt_words` ceiling
- a full pass covers every shot; a revision file covers a subset of real shots
- no shot block is duplicated, and none has a header with no body
- **Rule 1**: no on-screen text copy appears in any prompt
- **Rule 3**: `environment`, `lighting`, and `color_grade` appear verbatim, with the
  character anchor as a warning
- **Rule 6**: every shot states which third of the frame the body occupies, its point of
  view and its direction of travel; no scale contradictions, no two people at the same
  frame edge, no unnamed handedness in a two-person contact, no brand marks in frame

ubicaciones.encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar

registros.texto:
What it cannot check, and you still have to:

- [ ] One output file per requested generator
- [ ] On a revision pass, the shots you left out are accounted for as ACCEPT, post-only,
      or rejected, and you said which is which
- [ ] Generator-specific parameters are right for the surface the user will paste into
- [ ] The round is appended to `run.json` with a hash per prompt file
- [ ] The prompt actually describes the shot, which is the part no validator will ever do
